# LinkedIn post — PSYFORGE

*(attach the promo video `psyforge-promo.mp4` — its soundtrack was generated by the app itself)*

---

I'm a huge psytrance fan. So I built the festival in a browser tab.

Meet PSYFORGE 🎛️ — a beat maker where every single sound is synthesized live with the Web Audio API. No samples. No plugins. The kick is a pitch-swept sine. The rolling bassline is a saw through a filter. Even the "human voices" are three bandpass filters shaped like vowels.

What started as "can I make the Astrix roll in code?" turned into:

🎚️ A 9-track step sequencer with ratchets, step probability, swing and per-bar key changes
🌍 18 presets across 5 genre worlds — psytrance, trance, DnB, UK garage, phonk, amapiano, and yes, a proper bhangra dhol at 102 BPM
🎤 FRED MODE — record a 10-second voice note, it gets sliced onto pads, pitched, sequenced, and rendered into your export (Fred again.. workflow, fully in-browser)
🌀 A 4-style WebGL visualizer — kaleidoscope tunnel, hypno spiral, DMT maze, mandala — that dances to the actual audio signal
🥁 A BUILD button that queues a 2-bar snare roll and drops on the next bar, like it should
💾 WAV export rendered offline through the same synth graph

The wild part: the soundtrack of the video below was exported BY the app — 20 bars of its own Full-On Roller preset, key lift included.

Built end-to-end with Claude Code — from researching what makes a psy kick click at 1700 Hz, to the GLSL shaders, to this Remotion video.

Try it (headphones on): psyforge.vercel.app
Code: github.com/sisodiaravindra10/psyforge

## Shorter alt version

I built a psytrance beat maker that runs entirely in a browser tab.

Every sound is synthesized in real time with Web Audio — no samples. 18 genre presets (psy to amapiano to bhangra), a step sequencer with ratchets and probability, a WebGL visualizer, WAV export, and FRED MODE: record your voice, slice it onto pads, and sequence it into the track.

The video's soundtrack? The app exported it itself.

Built with Claude Code. Free and open source.
